_doc: Mammon's Clerk, Soul Broker of the Ledger. Nameless (he sold his name). Discovers that the Lattice's souls are being burned. Pool 'clerk' (shop ids: soul_broker, covenant).

lines.text: Ah! A customer! A debtor! Same thing, in the end.
Mammon's Clerk, at your service. No, I do not have a name. I sold it, years ago, at an excellent rate.
Souls deposited with the Ledger accrue interest. Bring them to me, and I will make them work harder than you do.

choices.text: And if I do not pay?

lines.label: cut
lines.text: Ha! Ha. Ha. You are funny. Mammon's cut is yes.

lines.label: pay
lines.text: Everyone pays, Sinbound. That is the entire premise of Hell. I just keep the receipts.
Deceased, re-formed, back in the queue. The Ledger records it all.
Your file is getting thick, {demon}. I have had to start a second folder.
Ten deaths! Do you know what the Ledger calls a demon who dies ten times?
What?
An investment. You keep coming back, and every time you come back, you are worth more.
Psst. Sinbound. Come closer. Closer than that. Mind the ink.
I have been running the old accounts. Souls in the mortal world are born, they die, they rise or fall. It balances. It always balances.
Except now it does not. The Lattice takes them, and they go nowhere. Not up, not down. Off the books.
In my profession, when money vanishes, it is being spent. Somebody is spending souls, Sinbound. A great many of them.
I found the line item. It took me eleven nights and one very unpleasant favour.
The souls the Lattice catches are being burned. Fuel, Sinbound. For a very large, very bright light.
The Last Dawn.
Heaven is lighting its sunrise with the dead. And they call us the monsters. Professionally, I am offended.
You want to know what I sold my name for? A chair. A seat at Mammon's own table. Very comfortable.
Worst trade I ever made. Never give up your name for a chair, Sinbound.

choices.text: And if the chair were very, very big?
I will keep that in mind.

lines.label: big
lines.text: ...Then that is a different calculation altogether. Let me find a bigger ledger.

lines.label: mind
lines.text: Do. Write it down. Writing it down is the only way anything is real.
A victory! Do you know how rarely I get to write that word in red ink?
Never. That is how rarely. I had to make the ink specially.
The Pale Reaper! Professional courtesy: your harvest figures are superb. Have you considered a pension?
I have considered you.
...Noted. Filed. Forgotten. Please.
Hexbinder. You collect names. I used to have one. Is it, by any chance, in your book?
It is. Would you like it back?
...What would it cost?
Everything you have.
Ha. Ha. No. I will keep being nobody. Nobody has excellent credit.
The Duchess Malphine owes the Ledger four thousand souls, a minor river and one firstborn imp.
So when the Court sends you to die gloriously, Sinbound, remember who is actually paying for it.
Interest compounds. So does damnation.
Spend wisely! Or do not. Either way, the Ledger profits.
Your account is in order. For now.
Every soul is a debt. Every debt is a soul. It is very elegant, if you do not think about it.
Another death? I will just add it to your tab.
{last.kills} angels in one outing. My quill can barely keep up.
I have been preparing an audit. Of Heaven. Every soul the Lattice burned, itemised, with interest.
When you take the chair, Sinbound, I would like to present it. Formally. With a ribbon.

choices.text: When I take the chair, you work for me.

lines.label: yes
lines.text: Oh! Oh, that is the nicest thing anyone has said to me since I had a name.

lines.label: mine
lines.text: Naturally. I work for whoever owns the ledger. That has always been the arrangement.
Ah, the former employee of the competition! Any insider information? I pay well.
Hexbinder. You still have my name? Keep it safe. It is worth more than you think. Or less.
Warden. Your prisoners' accounts are in arrears. Not your fault. Just mentioning.
Please do not charge the counter. The counter is the only thing I own.
Reaper! Your quarterly harvest report is a joy to read.
Nhazgul. Your account is... multiple. Do I bill each fly separately?
Ah, Iscariel! The Ledger has a whole department for your transaction. Thirty pieces. Very well documented.
Iscariel! I have a question that has bothered the Ledger for an age. Thirty pieces of light. Who paid them?
No one paid me, Clerk. I invented the price so they would think I could be bought. Nobody chases a man who sold out. They only chase the ones who believed.
...That is the most beautiful fraud I have ever heard. May I frame it?
